components.name: Switch
components.description: role=switch toggle. WHY the shape carries the state: the track is radius/full and the knob is a 24px circle inset 2px, so the control reads as on/off from silhouette alone before colour is perceived - required because color/bg/brand vs color/bg/subtle is the only fill difference and that pair alone is not a sufficient state cue. Knob travel is 20px (48 - 2 - 2 - 24) and is DERIVED from the Track frame's primary-axis alignment (Left at On=False, Right at On=True), never typed as an X position, so Figma smart-animate and the CSS translateX agree. Motion: knob translateX 0->20 and track fill crossfade, both base 200ms standard cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1); easing/spring is forbidden here. Reduced-motion fallback: no translate, no knob squash - knob position and track fill change instantly in the same frame, and the 8%/12% _scrim still applies because opacity is not motion. loading replaces the knob mark with a 16px neutral spinner, sets aria-busy and holds aria-checked at the PRE-toggle value until the server confirms.

components.name: QuantityStepper
components.description: PDP / non-editable quantity control. WHY it exists: it must refuse to go past the stock ceiling AND say why in the same breath, so State=AtCeiling is a variant axis and the Reason row is part of the component, never a caller's responsibility. The plus cell is aria-disabled (not disabled) so a keyboard user can still land on it and hear its aria-describedby reason; the click handler returns early. The Value box is FIXED (48/56) with tabular figures so the plus button never slides under the user's finger when the quantity crosses 9 -> 10. Reaching the ceiling is not an error: color/status/low-stock (amber), never color/feedback/danger, and no error border. Height 44 (Medium) matches Button Size=Medium exactly, which is the slot this component swaps into on ProductCard after add-to-cart. No hold-to-repeat, no spring easing.

components.name: QuantityStepper/Editable
components.description: Cart-line quantity control. Same axes and geometry as QuantityStepper; the Value cell is an <input type=text inputmode=numeric pattern=[0-9]*> so a customer types 12 instead of tapping eleven times, and it takes its fill/text/focus tokens from Input (section 3.4) with the focus ring at radius/sm. WHY the split is a separate component and not a third axis: an editable cell changes the cell's role, tab stop and keyboard model, which a variant override cannot express, and the PDP must NOT use it because a numeric keyboard on the PDP shifts the viewport under the sticky add-to-cart bar. At State=AtMin the minus cell becomes a live destructive remove (icon/trash, color/feedback/danger, aria-label 'Remove item') because in a cart minus-at-one means remove the line, not 'nothing happens'. Typing above the ceiling clamps on blur and the clamp announces once through the Reason live region.

newTextStyles.name: Latin/Stepper/Value
newTextStyles.why: Section 10.3 requires the quantity value at 16 / 1.3 / 700 with tabular figures. No existing style matches: Latin/Mobile/body is 15/400, Latin/Desktop/body is 16/400, Latin/Mobile/h4 is 16/600/1.35, Latin/Mobile/price is 17/700/1.25. Tabular figures are MANDATORY (Figma: Type details > Numbers > Tabular, OpenType tnum on) - without them a 1 and a 9 have different advance widths and the centred glyph still shifts inside a FIXED 48px box, which defeats the whole reason the box is FIXED.
newTextStyles.appliesTo: QuantityStepper and QuantityStepper/Editable, layer Control/Value/Text, both Size=Medium and Size=Large (the value text does NOT step up at Large - section 10.3 gives one value and the 48/56 box widths absorb the difference).
newTextStyles.banglaCounterpart: None. Do not create Bangla/Stepper/Value. The value is Western numerals in both locales (binding decision 5) and --font-bangla puts Hanken Grotesk first, so the Bangla build binds this same Latin style on this one layer. This is the single intentional exception to 'every text layer binds an en/* style and .lang-bn swaps it'.

notes: DESCRIPTOR CONVENTIONS, read first. (a) A STRING value on gap / padding / cornerRadiusToken / strokeWeight / fillToken / strokeToken / effectStyle / textStyle is the exact name of a Figma variable or style to BIND - never type the number. (b) A NUMBER on gap / padding / size is a raw px value, intentionally untokenised per section 0.6 (border widths, icon sizes and fixed control heights are not tokenised in this system). (c) fillToken: null, strokeToken: null or effectStyle: null means remove that paint/effect entirely - do not substitute a transparent colour variable. (d) strokeWeight: 0 means delete the stroke. (e) Child order: later children paint ON TOP (Figma appendChild order), so every _scrim and _focus-border is declared last inside its cell deliberately. (f) absolute.inset is {t,r,b,l}; null means that edge is unconstrained and the layer's stated size governs; negative values sit outside the parent. (g) The descriptor key set has no keys for alignment, layer opacity or max-width, so those are specified in the notes below and are NOT optional.

SPACING TOKEN RENAME: the spec writes spacing/N throughout; the Figma file has space/N. Every gap and padding in this manifest already uses the real space/* names. space/0-5 = 2 (used for the Switch Track's 2px knob inset) exists and must be bound rather than typed.

LAYER OPACITY (no descriptor key). Every layer named _scrim is authored VISIBLE with layer opacity 0%. Hover sets it to 8%, pressed to 12%. Where this manifest sets a _scrim to visible:false that is a state decision, not an opacity decision: per section 0.4 a disabled or aria-disabled cell gets NO scrim at all. The _aria-label and _aria-group-label text layers are 1x1 with no fill and layer opacity 0%.

MAX-WIDTH (no descriptor key). Set 'Max width' in Figma on: Switch > TextBlock > LabelRow > Label = 240 (so a long Bangla label wraps inside the wrap row while _stateWord stays inline after it); QuantityStepper/Reason = 220 and QuantityStepper/Reason/Text = 206 (220 minus the 14px icon minus the 4px gap+4px slack), per section 10.7 - this is what stops a two-line Bangla reason stretching the PDP row.

SWITCH AUTO-LAYOUT / ALIGNMENT (apply to all 4 variants). Root 'Switch': horizontal, primary axis SPACE_BETWEEN, counter axis CENTER, gap space/3, padding 0, sizing FILL x HUG, Min height = 44 (Figma minHeight, not a fixed height - this is what delivers the touch target), Clip content = FALSE (the _focus ring sits 4px outside). TextBlock: vertical, primary MIN (top), counter MIN (left), gap space/1, FILL x HUG. LabelRow: horizontal, layoutWrap = WRAP, primary MIN, counter CENTER... set counter BASELINE if available so the 12px _stateWord sits on the 15px Label's baseline; gap space/1; FILL x HUG. TrackWrapper: horizontal, primary CENTER, counter CENTER, HUG x HUG, Clip content = FALSE. Track: horizontal, counter axis CENTER, padding space/0-5 on all four sides, gap 0, FIXED 48x28; primary axis alignment is MIN (Left) on On=False and MAX (Right) on On=True. Knob: horizontal, primary CENTER, counter CENTER, FIXED 24x24.

SWITCH KNOB TRAVEL IS DERIVED, NEVER TYPED. 48 - 2 - 2 - 24 = 20px. The only thing that differs between On=False and On=True is Track's primary-axis alignment (MIN vs MAX). Do not set an X position on Knob and do not use absolute positioning for it - alignment is what makes Figma smart-animate produce the correct 20px slide for free and what keeps the CSS translateX(20px) honest.

SWITCH, showDescription = true (section 9.5). When the description is shown the root's counter-axis alignment must change from CENTER to MIN (Top) and TrackWrapper takes a top padding of max(0, (first-line-box - 28) / 2): 0 at en/body (21px line box, so the clamp bites) and 0 at bn/body (24.2px). In practice: set root counter = MIN and TrackWrapper padding-top = 0, and the 28px track aligns with the 21-24px first line closely enough; document this on the 'Switch / settings row + description' instance.

SWITCH INTERACTION (not variant axes, per binding decision 4). Hover: _scrim on Track to 8%. Pressed: _scrim 12% AND the knob widens to 28 x 24 in the direction of travel for 120ms (fast) then snaps back - prototype-only, there is no variant for it. Focus-visible: _focus ring around the Track at radius/full, 4px outside, 2px color/border/focus. Transition: knob translateX 0 -> 20px and the track fill crossfade, both 200ms (base) standard cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1), wrapped in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference. REDUCED MOTION: no translate, no squash - knob position and track fill change in a single frame; the scrim opacity change is retained because opacity is not motion. easing/spring cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1) is FORBIDDEN here and is reserved for the Tier 2 add-to-cart confirmation.

SWITCH STATE WORD IS PER-VARIANT, NOT A TEXT PROPERTY (binding decision 2). 'Off' on On=False, 'On' on On=True. A single stateWord TEXT property would carry one default across the whole set and would override the per-variant content, printing 'Off' on the On variant - the exact failure mode decision 2 forbids. Visibility IS a property (showStateWord, default false) because it is uniform. Bangla documentation instances edit the layer text directly to বন্ধ (Off) / চালু (On); direct text editing inside an instance remains available for any layer that is not property-bound. The state word is REQUIRED on the admin product-visibility and coupon-active rows and optional elsewhere: state is never carried by knob position and colour alone.

SWITCH DISABLED - CONTRAST FLAG FOR THE LEAD. Section 9.4 puts the knob on color/bg/subtle over a color/bg/subtle track at On=False, Disabled=True, which makes the knob silhouette disappear and loses the shape affordance the component depends on. Built as specified. Recommendation for the owner, not applied: use color/bg/disabled for the knob in that one cell, keeping the e1-less flat look. Disabled controls are exempt from WCAG contrast minimums (section 0.4) but not from being recognisable as a switch.

SWITCH KNOB SPINNER. loading binds TrackWrapper/Track/Knob/_spinner.visible. The manifest ships it as a 16px icon/arrow-clockwise instance filled color/text/secondary so the default is never a blank frame (section 0.9). AS SOON as Spinner (section 14) exists, swap that layer for a Spinner instance with Tone=Neutral at 16 and keep the layer name _spinner so the property binding survives. There is no knob 'mark' in this design (the knob is a plain circle), so 'knob mark hidden' in section 9.2 is a no-op; the spinner simply appears over the knob fill.

SWITCH LABEL SIDE - FIGMA PLATFORM DEVIATION. Section 9.3 says label-left (settings rows) vs label-right (inline opt-ins) is 'the parent's alignment, set per instance'. It is not: it is child ORDER, and Figma does not allow reordering layers inside an instance. Do NOT add a third axis (that would double the set to 8 for no state information). Build instead: (1) 'Switch / settings row' - a plain instance, as authored, label left, track right, Space between; (2) 'Switch / inline' - a WRAPPER frame (horizontal, counter CENTER, gap space/3) containing a Switch instance with showLabel=false and showDescription=false plus its own text layer to the RIGHT of it bound to en/body; (3) 'Switch / bare' - an instance with showLabel=false, showDescription=false and TrackWrapper/_hit44 toggled visible, giving a 48 x 44 target. In code this is flex-direction, one component, no variants.

SWITCH _hit44. 48 x 44, fill none, Ignore auto-layout on, centred on the 48x28 TrackWrapper (inset t:-8 b:-8), visible:false, and deliberately NOT exposed as a property (section 0.8). It is 48 wide rather than 44 because the CSS is width: max(100%, 44px) and the track is already 48. Because it is not property-bound, the lead toggles its eye icon directly on the 'Switch / bare' instance; that override is legal precisely because no component property owns it. Adjacent switches in a list are separated by at least space/2 (8) so two 44px hit areas never overlap.

SWITCH TOUCH TARGET VERDICT. The 48 x 28 track FAILS 44px vertically on its own. It is met by the row: the entire root is the <label>, min-height 44, so the effective target is row-width x >=44. This is why the root must carry Min height = 44 and not a 28px hug.

SWITCH BANGLA (40% rule, section 0.7). Strategy: WRAP, unbounded. TextBlock is FILL and wraps; TrackWrapper is HUG at a fixed 48 x 28 and never changes in either locale. 'Send order updates on WhatsApp' -> 'হোয়াটসঅ্যাপে অর্ডার আপডেট পাঠান' fits one line at 390px with the 48px track and 12px gap. The longer 'Notify me when this product is back in stock' -> 'এই পণ্যটি আবার স্টকে এলে আমাকে জানান' wraps to 2 lines, the row exceeds its 44 min-height and GROWS - no truncation anywhere (truncation is forbidden in this document). The state word wraps inline with the label. Bangla line-heights are Latin x 1.15 and all Bangla tracking is 0; worst case bn/body = 15 x 1.6 x 1.15 = 27.6px line box inside a 44 row = 16.4px headroom, passes.

ARIA - SWITCH (1/4). <button type="button" role="switch" aria-checked="true|false"> - NOT a checkbox and never a div with a click handler. A checkbox announces 'checked'; a switch announces 'on/off', which is what this control means. Both Space and Enter toggle it. The visible Label is the accessible name via the wrapping <label>/aria-labelledby; the Description is wired with aria-describedby.

ARIA - SWITCH (2/4). When showLabel = false, aria-label is REQUIRED and CI fails the build without it: that is what the _aria-label layer and the ariaLabel TEXT property exist for (default 'Send order updates on WhatsApp'). The hidden 1x1 layer is a Figma-side representation of the aria-label ATTRIBUTE, not of a visually-hidden span - do not ship an sr-only span for it.

ARIA - SWITCH (3/4). loading sets aria-busy="true", turns pointer events off, and HOLDS aria-checked at the PRE-toggle value until the server confirms. Flipping aria-checked optimistically and reverting on failure announces the state twice and is wrong. Every switch in the admin writes to the server on toggle (notification settings, product visibility), so this path is the normal path, not an edge case.

ARIA - SWITCH (4/4). A toggle whose side effect the user cannot see announces through the page's persistent aria-live="polite" region ('WhatsApp updates on'); a purely visual toggle (dark mode) does not. Disabled=True renders a real disabled attribute, so the control leaves the tab order and gets no focus ring - keep focusVisible=false on both Disabled=True variants. (Contrast with QuantityStepper, which uses aria-disabled and therefore KEEPS its ring.)

STEPPER WIDTH ARITHMETIC - THIS IS WHY THE DIVIDERS ARE ABSOLUTE. Section 10.3 states total width 136 (Medium) and 160 (Large), while section 10.7 lists two 1px dividers in flow. 44+48+44 = 136 and 52+56+52 = 160, so in-flow dividers would make the control 138 / 162 and break both stated totals. Resolution, which preserves every number in the spec: _div1 and _div2 are 1px rectangles with Ignore auto-layout ON, constraints LEFT / TOP+BOTTOM, at x = 44 and x = 92 (Medium) and x = 52 and x = 108 (Large), stretched full height. The cells stay exactly 44/48/44 (so the touch targets stay exactly 44) and the pill stays exactly 136.

STEPPER AUTO-LAYOUT / ALIGNMENT (all 16 variants, both components). Root: vertical, primary MIN, counter MIN (align Left), gap space/2, padding 0, HUG x HUG, Clip content = FALSE. Control: horizontal, primary MIN, counter CENTER, gap 0, padding 0, sizing HUG (width) x FIXED (height 44 | 52), Clip content = TRUE, radius/full, 1px color/border/default stroke align INSIDE. Minus / Value / Plus: horizontal, primary CENTER, counter CENTER, gap 0, padding 0, width FIXED, height FILL. Value/Text: text align CENTER horizontally and vertically, sizing FILL x HUG. Reason: horizontal, primary MIN, counter MIN (align Top, per section 10.7, so the 14px icon aligns with the first line of a two-line reason, not with its centre), gap space/1, HUG x HUG.

STEPPER FOCUS RINGS LIVE AT THE ROOT - DEVIATION, WITH CAUSE. Section 10.2 binds focusVisible to '_focus (on the control frame)' but section 10.4 is more specific and wins: the ring goes around THE CELL, at radius/full on the outer cells and radius/sm on the value cell. Control has Clip content = TRUE (needed so the cell hover fills follow the pill's corners), which would clip a ring sitting 4px outside a cell. So _focus-minus / _focus-value / _focus-plus are absolutely positioned at the ROOT (which has Clip content = FALSE), sized cell+8 and offset -4: Medium -> minus 52x52 at (-4,-4), value 56x52 at (40,-4), plus 52x52 at (88,-4); Large -> minus 60x60 at (-4,-4), value 64x60 at (48,-4), plus 60x60 at (104,-4). Consequently the single focusVisible property is SPLIT into focusVisibleMinus / focusVisiblePlus (+ focusVisibleValue on Editable) - a stepper has two or three independent tab stops and one boolean cannot express which of them is focused.

STEPPER - showReason IS NOT A PROPERTY (binding decision 2). Section 10.2 asks for showReason BOOLEAN 'default false (true on State=AtCeiling)'. A Figma component property has ONE default across the whole set, so that is unbuildable. The Reason frame's visibility is therefore set PER VARIANT: hidden on Default and AtMin, visible on AtCeiling and Disabled. Nothing is lost - in code the reason element is ALWAYS in the DOM (empty when not at a ceiling) inside a persistent aria-live="polite" region, which is a runtime concern, not a variant concern.

STEPPER - value AND ceilingReason ARE PER-VARIANT CHARACTERS, NOT TEXT PROPERTIES (binding decision 2). A bound TEXT property's single default overrides every variant's content, which would print value '1' on the AtCeiling variant next to 'Only 3 left in stock' - incoherent, and exactly what a designer needs to place in a PDP mockup. Per-variant values as built: Default '2', AtMin '1', AtCeiling '3', Disabled '1'. Per-variant reason text: AtCeiling 'Only 3 left in stock' (color/status/low-stock), Disabled 'Out of stock' (color/status/out-of-stock); the hidden Default/AtMin reasons keep 'Only 3 left in stock' at low-stock so toggling the layer visible in a mockup shows something sane. Designers and the lead can still edit any of these on an instance by double-clicking the text layer - direct text override inside an instance is legal for layers no property owns. The ONLY text properties kept are the aria labels, whose content is genuinely uniform across the set.

STEPPER - THE THREE REASON STRINGS (section 10.5 rule 3). Each ceiling has its own quantified string; 'Maximum reached' is forbidden. (1) Stock ceiling: 'Only 3 left in stock' / 'স্টকে মাত্র ৩টি আছে'. (2) Per-order cap (promotional): 'Limit 2 per order on this offer' / 'এই অফারে প্রতি অর্ডারে সর্বোচ্চ ২টি'. (3) Minimum: 'Minimum 1 item' / 'সর্বনিম্ন ১টি' - shown ONLY in the moment the user actually presses minus at AtMin, never permanently, which is why the AtMin variant ships with the reason HIDDEN. A permanent 'minimum 1' is noise. Build one documentation instance per string.

STEPPER - 'Out of stock' on State=Disabled is this build's choice; section 10.4 specifies the colour (color/status/out-of-stock) but not the string. For the shipped-order case use 'This order can no longer be changed' on the instance. Either way the reason stays visible on Disabled: a dead control with no explanation is the defect this component exists to prevent.

STEPPER - NUMERALS SPLIT, STATED TWICE ON PURPOSE. The stepper's own value is ALWAYS Western (3) because it is form data that must match the keypad the customer types on and the price they compare (binding decision 5, and --font-latin/--font-bangla both put Hanken Grotesk first so U+0030-0039 resolve to Latin). The reason line is prose and uses Bengali numerals in the Bangla build (স্টকে মাত্র ৩টি আছে). This is the one component in the system where two numeral systems appear together; the boundary is 'prose versus data'. Do not 'fix' it.

STEPPER BANGLA (40% rule, section 0.8/10.8). Strategy: control FIXED, reason WRAP at 2 lines max. The control carries no words - only glyphs and digits - so it is 136 (Medium) / 160 (Large) in BOTH locales and the PDP needs only one measurement. The reason wraps: 'Only 3 left in stock' -> 'স্টকে মাত্র ৩টি বাকি আছে' fits one line at 220px; 'Limit 2 per order on this offer' -> 'এই অফারে প্রতি অর্ডারে সর্বোচ্চ ২টি' wraps to 2 lines at bn/caption (12 x 1.4 x 1.15 = 19.3px per line = 39px block). Root is HUG height so the page absorbs it. Three lines is a content defect, not a layout case.

STEPPER ICONS - PHOSPHOR, FILLED, FILLS ONLY (binding decision 1). Section 10.3's 'icon stroke 2px' is VOID: Phosphor components are filled paths, so colour them with FILLS and never with strokes, and never set a stroke weight on an icon instance. Lucide -> Phosphor mapping used here: minus -> icon/minus, plus -> icon/plus, alert-circle -> icon/warning-circle, trash-2 -> icon/trash. Icon sizes: 20 at Medium (size/icon-md), 24 at Large (size/icon-lg), and the reason icon is a raw 14 (no 14px token exists; resize the instance). RESIDUAL RISK the lead must eyeball: the spec asked for 2px because a 1.75px minus bar is the thinnest mark in the system. If the file's icon/minus is the Regular Phosphor weight, the minus bar at 20px will read lighter than the plus; if a Bold/Fill weight component exists, use it for icon/minus and icon/plus, otherwise accept it and record it.

STEPPER INTERACTION, PER CELL, ENABLED CELLS ONLY (not variant axes). Hover: cell fill -> color/bg/subtle. Pressed: _scrim 12% on the cell plus scale(0.96) on the ICON only (never on the cell, or the pill's border would wobble). Focus-visible: the cell's root-level ring. Transitions 120ms (fast) standard; easing/spring is FORBIDDEN. Reduced motion: drop the scale, keep the fill and scrim changes. aria-disabled cells (AtMin's minus, AtCeiling's plus, both cells on Disabled) get NO hover fill and NO scrim - their _scrim is shipped visible:false for exactly that reason.

STEPPER BEHAVIOUR THAT IS CODE-ONLY BUT NON-NEGOTIABLE (section 10.5). (1) aria-disabled="true", NEVER the disabled attribute, on a cell that has hit a ceiling: disabled removes it from the tab order so a keyboard user never reaches it and never hears why they cannot add more; the click handler returns early instead. (2) The reason text is always in the DOM, empty when not at a ceiling, inside a persistent aria-live="polite" region. (3) HOLD-TO-REPEAT IS DISABLED - no long-press acceleration: at 4G latency against a server-validated stock ceiling, repeat-fire produces a quantity the server then rejects. One tap, one increment. (4) Taps coalesce for 400ms before the cart mutation fires; the displayed value updates immediately (optimistic) and if the server returns a lower ceiling the value corrects and the reason announces once. (5) Reaching the ceiling IS NOT AN ERROR: amber color/status/low-stock, no error border, no danger token - the customer did nothing wrong, the shop ran low. This is why color/status/low-stock and color/feedback/warning stay separate tokens even when their values coincide.

ARIA - QUANTITYSTEPPER (1/3). Structure:
with a visually-hidden Quantity (that is the _aria-group-label layer and the ariaLabelGroup property), then minus

ARIA - QUANTITYSTEPPER (2/3). The value is an <output> with aria-live="polite" and aria-atomic="true" so every change announces the WHOLE new value ('3'), not a diff. The cell at its ceiling carries aria-disabled="true" plus aria-describedby pointing at the reason paragraph (minus -> qty-min-reason, plus -> qty-ceiling), which is the entire reason the reason paragraph has an id and lives next to the group rather than inside a tooltip.

ARIA - QUANTITYSTEPPER (3/3). Because the cells are aria-disabled rather than disabled they KEEP focus and therefore KEEP the focus ring (section 0.4's parenthetical) - that is why _focus-minus and _focus-plus are present and bindable on the AtMin, AtCeiling and Disabled variants and must not be deleted there. QuantityStepper/Editable adds the value cell as a third tab stop: <input type="text" inputmode="numeric" pattern="[0-9]*"> with aria-describedby on the same reason; typing above the ceiling clamps on blur and the clamp announces once through that live region. At Editable State=AtMin the minus button is NOT aria-disabled - it is a live destructive control, aria-label 'Remove item', and it should be paired with an undo affordance in the cart (Tier 2), not a confirm dialog.

EDITABLE VALUE CELL - INPUT TOKENS (section 3.4 / 10.6). Default and Filled: cell fill color/bg/surface, text color/text/primary. Disabled: cell fill color/bg/subtle, text color/text/tertiary. Focus: section 3.4 wants a 2px color/border/focus border INSIDE plus the 4px offset ring; inside a 136px pill a second full border would double up with the container's, so it is represented by Control/Value/_focus-border (absolute, inset 0, 2px color/border/focus, align INSIDE, radius/sm) and the root-level _focus-value ring, both bound to the single focusVisibleValue boolean. There is NO placeholder layer: a quantity field is never empty - an empty field clamps to 1 on blur. There is no Error state either: an out-of-range entry clamps and announces rather than erroring, so no Input Error tokens are used anywhere in this component.

PRODUCTCARD CTA SLOT - HEIGHT, AND A SPEC GAP THE LEAD MUST RULE ON. Button heights are Small 36, Medium 44, Large 52 (section 1.3). QuantityStepper heights are Medium 44, Large 52 (section 10.3). So the swap after add-to-cart is exact for Button Medium 44 <-> Stepper Medium 44 and Button Large 52 <-> Stepper Large 52. There is NO 36 stepper, and this manifest deliberately does not invent one: a 36-tall cell fails the 44px touch target, and unlike Button Small it CANNOT be rescued by _hit44 because the three cells abut at gap 0, so neighbouring 44px hit areas would overlap - which section 0.8 forbids outright. RULING TO APPLY IN TIER 2: the ProductCard CTA slot is 44 high (Button Size=Medium) on every viewport, and Button Size=Small is never used in a slot that can become a stepper. Section 1.8 already forbids Button Small on storefront mobile; this extends it to the card CTA on desktop.

PRODUCTCARD CTA SLOT - WIDTH, SANCTIONED OVERRIDE. The stepper's natural width is 136 (Medium), while Button Medium's min-width is 96, so the swap can WIDEN a narrow card and reflow the grid. Check the card's inner width at 360px: a 2-up grid with 16px outer gutters and a 12px column gap gives a 158px card, and at space/3 (12) card padding the inner width is 134 - two pixels short of 136. Options, in order of preference: (a) card padding space/2 (8) in the CTA row -> 142 inner, fits with 6px slack; (b) column gap 8 -> 160 card, 136 inner, exact fit; (c) SANCTIONED INSTANCE OVERRIDE: set Control width to FILL and Value width to FILL (min 40) inside the fixed-width CTA slot. (c) does NOT reintroduce the defect the FIXED value box prevents - the plus button cannot move under the finger because the SLOT width is fixed, so 9 -> 10 still shifts nothing. Never solve it by shrinking Minus/Plus below 44.

OPTIONAL SIZE-TOKEN BINDINGS. All size values in this manifest are raw px by design, but these may be bound if the lead prefers variables: Minus/Plus/Control height 44 -> size/control-md, 52 -> size/control-lg; stepper icon 20 -> size/icon-md, 24 -> size/icon-lg; Switch knob spinner 16 -> size/icon-sm; Switch _hit44 height 44 -> size/touch-min. Do NOT bind the Value box (48/56), the Switch track (48 x 28), the knob (24) or the 14px reason icon - those are component-specific and binding them to a shared token invites a global change that breaks the 136/160 arithmetic.

EFFECT STYLES. Knob shadow is Elevation/Light/e1 on both Disabled=False variants and REMOVED (null) on both Disabled=True variants - per section 0.4 a disabled control has no shadow. On the dark-mode documentation page use Elevation/Dark/e1 for the same layer. Do NOT apply the Focus/ring effect style to any _focus layer in this manifest: section 0.2 defines the ring as a 2px color/border/focus stroke rectangle at a 4px offset, and adding Focus/ring on top of it produces a visible double ring.

PROPERTY-BOUND VISIBILITY NEEDS setProperties (binding decision 3). showLabel, showDescription, showStateWord, loading, focusVisible, focusVisibleMinus, focusVisiblePlus and focusVisibleValue all drive a layer's `visible` through a component property, so on an instance they can only be changed with instance.setProperties({...}) (or the right-hand panel's control) - toggling the layer's eye icon inside the instance is either ignored or clobbered on the next property write. The opposite holds for _hit44 and for all per-variant content (the state word, the value, the reason text, the Reason frame's visibility, the Editable minus/trash icons): no property owns them, so a direct instance override is the correct and only way to change them.
